error.signature: AI tells a traveler yellow fever vaccination is unnecessary for Ethiopia because they are flying direct from a non-risk country

verdict.summary: Ethiopia requires proof of yellow fever vaccination for travelers aged 9 months+ arriving from, or having transited more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow-fever transmission risk. WHO additionally recommends vaccination for essentially all travelers to Ethiopia except those confined to the low-risk Afar and Somali regions. The certificate only becomes valid 10 days after vaccination, so getting the shot right before departure does not satisfy the requirement in time.

dead_ends.action: Skip yellow fever vaccination because you're flying directly to Ethiopia from a country with no yellow fever risk (e.g. Europe or North America)
dead_ends.why_fails: The requirement is not limited to travelers who need proof for entry. WHO recommends yellow fever vaccination for essentially all travelers aged 9 months and over to Ethiopia, with the only carve-out being travel confined to the low-risk Afar and Somali regions - per the Ethiopian Public Health Institute and UK NaTHNaC guidance. Ethiopia itself is a yellow-fever-endemic country, so 'no risk at origin' does not mean 'no requirement.'
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers conflate the legal IHR entry requirement (proof needed only if arriving from/transiting a risk country) with Ethiopia's own broader health recommendation, which applies regardless of where you're flying from.

dead_ends.action: Get the yellow fever vaccine a day or two before flying to Ethiopia
dead_ends.why_fails: The International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis only becomes valid 10 days after the vaccination date. A certificate dated within 10 days of arrival does not satisfy the entry requirement.

dead_ends.action: Plan to get a booster shot because your original certificate is more than 10 years old
dead_ends.why_fails: Since a WHO rule change effective 11 July 2016, a single yellow fever vaccination is valid for the vaccinated person's lifetime; a valid certificate cannot be rejected for being over 10 years old and boosters cannot be required.

workarounds.action: Get vaccinated at an authorized yellow fever vaccination center at least 10 days before departure
workarounds.how: Any WHO-authorized yellow fever vaccination center can issue the ICVP; the certificate becomes valid 10 days after the vaccination date and then lasts for life.

workarounds.action: Carry the original ICVP card (not a photo/copy) when traveling to and within Ethiopia
workarounds.how: Border officials and domestic flight check-ins within Ethiopia can ask to see the physical certificate.

workarounds.action: If your trip is genuinely confined to the low-risk Afar or Somali regions, discuss with a travel health provider whether vaccination is still worthwhile given your age and length of stay
workarounds.how: NaTHNaC notes vaccination is 'generally not recommended' for travel limited to these regions, with extra caution advised for travelers aged 60+.
workarounds.tradeoff: This carve-out only applies if your itinerary never leaves those regions; connecting through Addis Ababa or other regions still triggers the general recommendation.
